notes.headline: New game: Link Up
details: Sixteen words, four hidden groups, a new puzzle every day
Same daily puzzle for both of you: share your result to compare
Word Rattle is back to its original name

notes.headline: Link Up: bonus puzzles and make your own
details: 30 bonus puzzles you can play any time, plus every past daily puzzle.
Make your own board: four groups of four words, in the four colours.
Tap Send to share your board as a link. Whoever taps it gets it in Link Up.
Boards sent to you appear under Shared with you.
Words on the tiles are a readable size again.

notes.headline: Link Up: times for every colour
details: After each puzzle, see how long each colour took you to find.
New Times card: average and fastest solve, total time, and average and fastest time for each colour.
Switch the Times card between daily puzzles and all puzzles.
The clock now pauses when you leave a puzzle, and your shared result includes your colour times.

notes.headline: Gem Tower Defence: rage, handicaps and four new gems
details: Four new gem colours: Onyx grows with every hit, Peridot's hits jump between enemies, Aquamarine stops healing and shields, Pearl hits harder the more coins you save.
Rage button under the map: tougher waves that pay more coins and earn shards.
Handicaps: optional harder rules that add to every shard you earn. They open after you clear the first map.
New players start with Ruby and unlock the other colours with shards. Your six colours are kept.
Master each colour, and five new upgrades in the Forge.
Enemies are tougher, especially after wave 30.

notes.headline: Word Rattle: Swap letters
details: New game option: Swap letters. Every word you make swaps its letters for new ones, so the board keeps changing.
Turn it on in the game settings before you create a board.
Send the board to each other as usual: you both get the same new letters if you find the same words in the same order.
Comparing a swap game shows points and word counts. Each board ends up different, so there's no word-by-word list.

notes.headline: New game: Topple
details: Tip a long block end over end and drop it standing up into the hole.
30 levels, from gentle to fiendish, with fragile tiles, switches and bridges.
A new daily puzzle every day, the same for both of you. Weekends are bigger.
Swipe or use the arrows. Undo and Hint are there when you're stuck.

notes.headline: New game: Mudlark
details: A white labradoodle, a big mud slope, and the seaside 3 km away.
Slide, launch off the lip and tilt the nose with the arrows to glide.
Catch floating bone treats, earn more for distance, height and speed, and hit goals for bonuses.
Spend treats on a taller slope, slicker mud, sleds, wings and boosters, all the way to a jet pack.

notes.headline: New game: Boxed In
details: Hold out against waves of zombies and fireball-throwing devils.
Drag on the left to walk. Your gun aims and fires by itself.
Score unlocks an uzi, shotgun, barrels, grenades, barricades and rockets.
Three arenas: survive wave 8 to open the next one.

notes.headline: Mudlark is now Buddy Breakout
details: The doodle is Buddy now, and he's heading for a group of lady dogs in the dog park, 3 km away.
Land next to them to finish. Fly straight past and Buddy panics.
Your days, treats and kit are all kept.

notes.headline: Boxed In: smoother controls
details: Fixed a wave that could never end because zombies got stuck in a doorway
You can no longer get trapped inside your own barricade
The thumb stick works anywhere on the screen and responds straight away
Barrels and barricades drop with one tap, behind you as you run, and your gun keeps firing

notes.headline: New game: Echo Cartographer
details: A maze in total darkness. Tap to send out a ping and the walls light up for a moment, then fade.
You only get a few pings, so remember the layout and steer your dot to the green exit.
30 levels and a new maze every day.

notes.headline: Echo Cartographer: Restart moved
details: The Restart button is now the ↻ at the top, away from the arrows, so it's harder to tap by accident.

notes.headline: New game: Buddy's Big Slide
details: Draw a track with your finger, press Play, and Buddy rides his sledge down it.
15 challenges: reach the flag, catch the bones, and use as little ink as you can for three stars.
A new daily slide every day, the same for both of you. Fewest ink wins.
Draw your own tracks with loops, jumps and orange boost lines, and send them to each other as a link.

notes.headline: Topple: endless climb and 45 new levels
details: Endless climb: board after board, each a bit harder, the same boards for both of you. Finish each within its move limit or lose a heart. Three hearts, and every 5 boards wins one back.
45 new levels (now 75) with three new tiles: crumbly tiles that fall away behind you, ice that slides you along, and purple pads that teleport you across the board.

notes.headline: New game: Lee Lee's Kitchen
details: Run a café, bakery and deli, or a restaurant and pub, as Lee Lee.
Take orders, cook (chop, stir and pour yourself), serve, clear tables and wash up. Burnt food and slow service cost you.
Pubs get busy and rowdy late at night: calm people down and mop up the spills.
Each evening in the office: buy stock, learn recipes, hire and promote staff, buy equipment, advertise, and move somewhere bigger.
Five save slots, and you can rename your place any time.

notes.headline: New game: Gravity Well
details: Launch a ball and let the planets bend it round to a target that's usually out of view.
Every planet pulls, harder the closer you get. Pink ones push you away, and moons circle as you fly.
30 levels, plus a new daily orbit every day that's the same for both of you.
Drag to aim, then fine-tune with the buttons. Tap Map to see the whole level.

notes.headline: New game: Epoch Siege
details: Your base on the left, the enemy's on the right: train troops and knock their base down first.
Six ages, from the Stone Age to the Future Age. Beat enemies to earn experience, then evolve for far stronger troops, defences and a tougher base.
Five kinds of troop in every age, including healers and a champion that smashes bases. Units that win three fights become veterans.
Defences for your base, six upgrades that go up to ten levels, a special attack for each age, and orders to charge, hold or fall back.
Four enemy levels, from Easy to Brutal. The battle saves itself, so you can leave and carry on later.

notes.headline: Epoch Siege: a tougher enemy and crowd fighting
details: Every enemy level is harder. Normal now earns more gold and experience than you, defends its base properly, and catches up quickly if you get an age ahead.
If you still find it easy, try Hard or Brutal.
New option, Crowd fighting: troops bunch up three at a time, so more of them fight at once instead of waiting in a line.

notes.headline: New game: Hollowdeep
details: Dig out an underground realm and beat the rival lords, in the spirit of the old dungeon-building games.
You don't steer anyone: mark rock to dig and build rooms. Your diggers and creatures get on with it themselves.
Lairs, mushroom farms, treasuries, training pits and libraries attract Beetles, Goblins, Hexers and Ogres through your Gate.
Plant a flag to send your creatures to fight, or pick them up and drop them where you want them.
Six realms to conquer, plus quick games against 1 to 3 rivals. Your game saves itself.

notes.headline: Epoch Siege: campaign, generals and perks
details: A 12-mission campaign, each battle with its own twist: heavies only, survive the clock, no gold over time, a fortress with double walls, and more. Every mission has three stars to earn.
Stars and battle wins earn medals. Spend them in the new Barracks on 13 perks, each going up to level 3, and take three into any battle.
Seven generals to unlock, each with a strength and a weakness: the Builder, the Raider, the Sage, the Mender and more.
Balance: healers can no longer stack on one troop, shooters now aim for enemy healers first, Hard is a bit tougher and Brutal a bit kinder.

notes.headline: Epoch Siege: three lanes, a longer campaign and general levels
details: Three-lane battles: tap a lane and it glows, and everything you train marches down it until you pick another. Defences cover all three lanes. Turn it on in Battle, and many new missions use it.
Map view: a button on the battlefield switches to a view from above, with your base at the bottom.
The campaign now has 30 missions, then splits into three roads (the Iron Road, the Wild Frontier and the Three Fronts) before a final battle.
Generals now level up to 5 by leading battles, getting stronger and losing their weakness. Three new generals, plus three more waiting at the end of each road.
Four new perks: Long Bows, Repair Crews, Bargain Hunter and Heavy Drill.

notes.headline: Lee Lee's Kitchen: campaign, worktops and easier tapping
details: New campaign: 25 days from a corner café to a restaurant, each teaching one thing, with three stars to earn.
Tapping is more precise: tap anywhere near a station and Lee Lee goes to it, with a dashed outline showing where she's heading.
Put anything down on the six counter spots or a worktop, and pick it up again. Each new place starts with a worktop.
The office is simpler: four tabs (Today, Menu, Team, Upgrades), and stock is topped up for you each night.
People already queueing at closing time now stay to be served.

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: room shapes, a Workshop, traps and doors
details: Shapes matter: a 2×2 or 3×3 square of a room becomes something special, like a Book stand, a Vault, a Big nest, a Sparring ring or a Great forge. Tap a room to see what its shapes do.
Four new rooms: Workshop, Shrine, Guard room and Crypt. They bring Tinkers, healing Spirits and Skeletons who need no pay.
The Workshop makes doors (wood, iron, warded) and traps (spike pits, rolling boulders, flame vents, lightning runes and alarm bells). Plan them, and your diggers make and fit them.
Rival lords now build their own doors and traps, so bring something heavy.
Every room looks different now: beds, mushrooms, bookshelves, candles and bones vary from tile to tile.

notes.headline: Gravity Well: Deep Space, Star Run and Voyage
details: 30 new Deep Space levels (31-60): crowded systems where there is never a simple way round.
New things in space: black holes that pull hard and swallow the ball, and wormholes that send it out of a matching one.
Star Run: 30 levels where you pick up every gold star in one shot before the target opens.
Voyage: an endless run of systems, each harder, from a shared tank of 10 shots. A hole in one earns 3 more.
From tomorrow the daily orbit is a crowded system too, and some days have stars to collect.

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: spells, possession, prisoners, heroes and 15 realms
details: Spells: Lightning and Possess from the start, and your Library researches Heal, Sight, Haste, Call to arms and Cave-in. Mana flows in faster the more floor you own.
Possess a creature and fight with it yourself, with a thumb stick and an attack button.
Build a Jail and beaten enemies are knocked out, not killed. Your diggers lock them up, and a Persuasion room wins them over to your side: heroes and wild beasts too.
Heroes now come down from the surface in waves, with a Dwarf digging the way and a Hero Champion at the end.
15 realms with three stars each, bigger maps, lava rivers, underground lakes, crystal caverns, natural tunnels, lost creatures to recruit, wild beasts and treasure hidden in the rock.
Diggers work together: up to three on each side of a rock. They claim floor in neat rows now.

notes.headline: Lee Lee's Kitchen: a helping hand, goals and difficulty
details: A green arrow shows what to do next while you learn, and pops up later if you seem stuck (Settings: Auto, Always or Off).
Tap an order on the strip at the top and Lee Lee goes straight to it.
After every day: a tip on what would help most next time.
Free play: choose Relaxed, Normal or Busy, and each day has two goals worth a bonus.
Happy tables in a row build a 🔥 streak with bigger tips. Rush warnings, and sounds (including beeps before food burns).
Campaign: stuck on a day? After two tries you can have an easier go. Finishing a chapter earns a certificate worth £75 in free play.

notes.headline: A tidier games list
details: Today's puzzles at the top: see at a glance which daily games you've done today, and tap one to play.
Carry on: the last two games you played sit just below, ready to jump back in.
Games are now in smaller tiles, grouped into Words & numbers, Puzzles, Strategy, and Action & easy-going.
Backup and Check for updates are folded away at the bottom: tap Backup & app updates to open them.

notes.headline: Word Rattle and Kakuro in Today's puzzles
details: Today's puzzles on the games list now includes the Word Rattle daily board and Kakuro's puzzle of the day.
If you'd already played them today, open each game once and the tick appears.

notes.headline: Link Up: trickier puzzles
details: From tomorrow's puzzle (#12), the daily Link Up is harder: lots of words look like they fit two or three groups, but only one way works.
A month of new puzzles. Earlier puzzles and your streak are unchanged.

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: rival lords that grow and conquer
details: Rival lords now play more like people: each has a personality (builder, raider or schemer), keeps digging out a bigger realm all game, and spends their gold.
They gather their army at the border before attacking, march together, and fall back to regroup when a fight goes badly. You get a warning when an army is gathering.
Lords fight each other too: a strong lord picks on the weakest neighbour and takes over their land, so leave one alone and it snowballs.
When enemies get into your realm, your creatures drop what they're doing and turn out together to fight.
Beat a rival and their realm, rooms and all, becomes yours.
The Jail and Persuasion room have proper art now: iron cells, a fireside with armchairs and a great hall.

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: a different start every time
details: You no longer always start bottom left: it can be any corner or the middle of any side, with your rivals spread out from you.
Your first hall comes in different shapes and sizes, the first Gate lies in a different direction, and gold turns up in different places.
There's always something different close by: a gem seam, a lost creature, buried treasure, a little pool or an outcrop of hard rock.

notes.headline: New game: Life
details: Start as a tiny cell in a pond: eat, dodge the hunters, and grow through five sizes.
Design your own creature: mouths, tails, eyes, thorns, shells, colours and markings. Every creature in the pond is different, and so is yours.
Find glowing pods for new body parts, and meet your mate to evolve.
Play Normal (come back when you're eaten) or Hardcore (one life only).
This is the cell stage. The sea stage, and the stages after it, come in later updates.

notes.headline: Life: smarter creatures and parts that matter
details: The other creatures don't swim in circles any more: plant eaters graze and stick together, and hunters get hungry, chase prey their size, switch to a better meal if one swims past, then eat what they catch.

Every body part now does something where you put it, good and bad. Tails only push when they point backwards, each jaw bites on its own, shells only protect their own side, and every part adds weight.
Tap a part in the builder to see what it's good and bad at.
Glowing pods show which part is inside, and creatures you beat sometimes drop one of their own parts. Pick them up and use them if you like.
Four new parts to find: Pincer, Bristles, Paddle and Clear skin.

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: a 20-realm campaign that builds up step by step
details: The campaign is now 20 realms that start simple and add one thing at a time: the first realm has just Lairs, farms, treasuries and Beetles.
Each realm brings something new, like Training pits and Goblins, Possession, the Library and spells, the Workshop and traps, prisoners, Spirits, heroes and finally Ogres and the Great forge.
Things you haven't reached yet show a lock and the realm they arrive in. Rival lords play by the same rules.
Every realm opens with a briefing: what's new, your goal and the two bonus stars.
Realms 15 to 20 use everything, with bigger maps, fiercer lords and longer hero sieges.

notes.headline: Life: choose where to start
details: When you start a new life you can now jump straight to Droplet size, Titan size, or the very end of the cell stage, with every part and plenty of DNA. Handy for trying things out.
Lives started this way are marked "Test start" on the menu. The sea stage and the stages after it will join the list as they're built.

notes.headline: Life: the sea stage, and easier part picking
details: The sea is here! Finish the pond and tap Into the sea: your creature grows a longer body that bends as it swims.
Dive from the sunlit shallows through the kelp reef and open blue to the twilight and the pitch-dark Deep. The deeper you go, the bigger the food and the danger. A little map shows where you are.
Your nest is where you evolve. Each time you grow, it hatches young that swim with you and join your fights.
Your diet slides towards what you eat: stay in the middle eating both, or become a plant eater or meat eater.
Ten new sea parts, including tail fins, beaks, tentacles, ink clouds, armour and lamps for the dark. Goals to chase, and giants in the Deep.
At the last size, grow lungs and two leg fins and crawl up onto the shore.
In the builder, tap a part's name in the new list to pick it, then drag anywhere to move it. You can also nudge it round the body with the arrow buttons.

notes.headline: Life: the land stage
details: Crawl out of the sea and tap Onto the land: your fins become legs, and you explore an island made just for your species.
Tap the ground to walk there, drag to look around, pinch or use + and − to zoom. Tap bushes and fruit trees to eat.
Tap a creature to meet it, then choose Hunt, Impress or Leave. To impress, copy its show: 🎵 call, 💃 dance, 🦚 show off, 💪 pose. The right parts (voice sacs, legs, crests, horns) score better.
Win over three of a species to make friends (one may join your pack), or hunt four to drive it off the island. Two giants roam too.
Your pack follows you and fights beside you; tap 📣 then a creature to send them after it. In fights, tap 💥 charge, 🐾 pounce, 💦 spit or 📣 roar.
Day turns to night, when some hunters come out. Eleven new land parts, including legs, hands, horns, claws, crests, ears and little wings.
Every species you deal with grows your brain. A full brain makes your species clever enough for the tribe stage, coming later.

notes.headline: Life: a whole new land stage
details: The island is seen at an angle now, more like 3D: trees, palms, pines, cacti and rocks stand up and cast shadows, hills are shaded, and creatures walk on their legs.
A bigger island with beaches, meadows, forests, jungle, swamp, dry scrub, hills, cliffs, snowy peaks, lakes and rivers.
Fog: you only know the beach at first, and the map fills in as you explore. You see creatures only when they're close, so eyes, ears and a long neck help.
Ten places to discover, like the Great Falls, Hot Springs (they heal you) and a Field of Bones (part pods). Each adds to your brain.
Animals live differently now: herds roam the island and panic together, hunting packs roam and attack as one, some animals live alone, and homebodies stay by their nest and defend it.
Twelve species to meet, from little six-legged critters to long-necked giants, plus birds, butterflies and fireflies.
Leftover sea parts (fins and the like) are dead weight on land. They're gone from the builder; tap one on your creature to evolve it away.
If you'd already started the land stage, you're on the new island: your brain, DNA, pack and design are kept, but the species tally starts again.

notes.headline: Life: the land stage is now real 3D
details: The island is built in 3D: mountains rise with rock cliffs and snowy tops, lakes sit in hollows, rivers run downhill, and waves meet the beach.
Trees, bushes, rocks and the ten special places are proper 3D models with sunlight and shadows. Fruit and berries disappear as they're eaten and grow back.
Every creature, including yours, is built in 3D from its design, in its own colours and markings. Legs really walk, tails sway, jaws snap and voice sacs puff.
Hunters have angry brows, slit eyes and sharp teeth, and their eyes glow at night.
Day turns to an orange evening and then a dark night, with a glow round you so you can still see.
If a tree or hill is in front of you, you show through it as a faint outline.
Pinch or use + and - to zoom, and drag to look around, as before. On an older phone the picture gets a little softer to keep things smooth.

notes.headline: Life: the thumb stick stays put
details: In the cell and sea stages the thumb stick now stays where you first put your thumb, instead of following it round the screen.
Push past the edge of the ring for full speed in that direction.

notes.headline: Life: tougher animals that stick together
details: Every kind of animal on the island now has a temperament, shown when you meet one: shy ones all run when trouble starts, defenders all turn on whoever attacks one of them, and aggressive ones come for you if you get close.
Groups act together: hunt one and the rest of its herd, pack or nest either scatters or gangs up on you.
Defenders and aggressive kinds hit much harder and take more beating, so pick your fights and bring your pack.
Nests: empty an animal's nest (drive them off or beat them) and walk in to claim it, for DNA, a little brain, and eggs or a new part.
Fewer trees in the woods, and taller ones, so it's easier to see what's going on under them.

notes.headline: Life: the volcano, the great migration, and goals on land
details: Partway through the land stage the ground starts shaking. Then the mountain erupts and fire spreads across the island. Run for the green light on safe ground and keep your pack with you.
Every animal flees too. Afterwards they all settle on new ground near your new nest, and the old land is left burnt, with blackened trees.
Later, a fierce new pack comes ashore. Beat three of them for a goal.
Stampedes: now and then a herd comes charging straight through. Get out of the way!
Ten land goals to tick off (see the pause menu), each worth 25 DNA and a part pod.
Even fewer trees in the woods, so you can see through them.

notes.headline: Life: shape your creature in 3D
details: On land, the builder has a new Shape tab: raise the head for a neck, lift the front to stand up on two legs, and make each body section tall and deep or low and flat. Stretch or squash the spine too. Shaping is free.
Pick any part to change its size, and change the length of legs, tails, necks, horns, eye stalks, feelers, arms and claws.

Size and length matter: long legs stride faster but turn slower and weigh more, really long ones reach fruit in the trees, bigger jaws and horns hit harder, and every bigger part is heavier and costs more DNA.
A 3D preview of your creature turns slowly in the corner of the builder while you work. Drag it to spin it round.

The island's animals come in proper body shapes now: long-legged browsers with raised necks, low flat crawlers, round little grazers, deep-chested herds, hunched hunters with long tails, and upright two-legged runners.

notes.headline: Life: the Tribe stage
details: Finish the land stage and your species starts a tribe on the same island. Tap Start a tribe.
You're the Chief: tap to walk as before. Your villagers work on their own. Tap Jobs to choose who chops wood, digs stone, fetches materials, hunts, builds or guards. Everyone else gathers food.
Build huts so the tribe can grow, totems to claim more land, and watch fires to guard it. Villagers only gather inside your land.
Fires burn wood and buildings need mending every minute, and your stores only hold so much, so keep enough people chopping wood and digging stone.
Explore to find flint, clay and reeds, claim them with a totem, and bring them home to make tools: axes, spears, baskets, pots, shields and slings.

Four neighbouring tribes share the island. Win over the friendly ones with gifts, trade and a show for their chief. At friendship 60 they become your allies and send warriors to help, and at 100 they join you.

Hostile tribes raid your camp. Break their spirit to make them give in: hem them in with your land and your allies' land, beat their raids, burn their totems, raid their stores or beat their champion in a duel.
Send a founding party to start a new camp far from your others, with land of its own.
Settle all four neighbours to finish the stage. To try it straight away, start a new life and pick Tribe stage under Start at.
Land stage: creatures are smaller and the camera is closer in, so the island feels bigger. When the volcano erupts, the camera pulls back so you can see where to run.

notes.headline: Life: no more crash when beating a big animal
details: On land, the game no longer crashes just as you beat an animal bigger than you, such as one from a big herd.

notes.headline: Life: land fixes
details: After the eruption, animals and giants no longer all crowd round your nest. Each kind goes off to its own new home, and the giants live well away. This also fixes games where it already happened.
Tapping an animal works much better: tap anywhere on its body, legs included, even on tall ones.
When something attacks you, you now bite back on your own, and there's a Fight back button to go after it properly (as well as Run and your moves).

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: old places, surprises, rare creatures and better-looking rooms
details: Rooms look like rooms now: floors run across the whole room (planks, big slabs, raked sand, carpets), the back wall has shelves, weapon racks, banners and torches, and there are many more bits of furniture, spread out thinly.

Old places are hidden in the rock, about halfway between you and your rivals. Beat a Sealed tomb's guardians to take its treasure. Hold a Mana spring, War idol, Mother lode or Healing well for a lasting boost. Rivals hunt for them too, and will try to take yours.
Surprises every few minutes: a tremor opens a new tunnel, a rockfall bares a gold seam, beasts burst into somebody's realm, or sell-swords camp in the rock for whoever reaches them first.

Five rare creatures that come only when something unusual is true of your realm: the Shade (a spy who slips into rival realms and steals their gold), Wyrm, Ghoul, Sporeling and Ember imp. Rivals can get them too: Watchtowers, alarm bells and guards spot Shades.
You now choose your army: tap the creature count at the top to see what each kind needs, and to turn kinds away from your Gates.
Games already in progress carry on as they were, and get the surprises. Old places appear in new games (from the second realm on).

notes.headline: Hollowdeep turns darker: torture, sacrifice, chosen research and sound
details: A darker mood: places you can't see lie in shadow, the dark closes in round the screen, blood stays where things die, and a voice in the dark comments on how you're doing.
Sound for the first time: a low drone, your Heart beating (faster when it's hurt), digging, fighting, spells and screams. Turn it off from the ☰ menu.

Torture chamber: breaks prisoners much faster than persuasion, and a broken rival's creature gives away the map of its old realm. Some don't survive. Build squares for a Rack or a Wheel of pain. It brings a new creature, the Tormentor.

Three more rooms: the Fighting pit (free levelling, but it hurts), the Gambling den (cheers creatures up and earns you gold) and the Dark altar (sacrifice a creature for mana, research and a mended Heart).
You choose what your Library studies: tap Spells, then Study. Known spells can be mastered to cost less mana. Three new spells: Curse, Raise the dead and Hellfire.
Creatures grow bigger as they level up, and diggers now level up from working: faster digging and claiming, and bigger loads.

notes.headline: Hollowdeep: The Long Dark, a whole new campaign
details: A second campaign, on Hollowdeep's front page. You have one keep that lasts the whole war: nothing you build there is thrown away.

A war map of sixteen realms. Choose where to march, pick which creatures go, and bring the survivors home as named veterans with the gold. Each realm teaches you its rooms, creatures and spells, and the best are furthest away.
Three rival lords take realms on the map as you do. The more a lord holds, the bigger the army you meet. Take a lord's own seat to finish them.
Three ways to end a realm: destroy the Heart, starve the lord by holding every Gate, or spare them when they beg and take tribute every turn.

Dread: conquest, torture, sacrifice and raids make the surface fear you. Heroes come for your keep after every expedition. Raid the surface yourself: sack a village, burn the abbey that trains Clerics, or break the heroes' castle.
Rockfalls: the bigger you dig, the more often open, empty floor fills in again. You get a warning, and rooms hold the roof up.
In the Long Dark, the richest gold, gems, treasure and tombs lie furthest from your Heart.

notes.headline: Life: tribe fixes for stone and guards
details: Villagers no longer get stuck in a tangle with each other: they walk past one another now.
Stone diggers spread out over the rocks, skip rocks stuck inside cliffs, and will walk a little way out of your land if there's no stone inside it.
Guards walk the rounds of your fires, watch fires and totems, and go after raiders and anything attacking your people anywhere in your land, instead of standing still.
Tap 📣 to take your guards on a raid: they follow you and fight any enemy tribe's people near you, in their land too. Tap 📣 again to send them home.

notes.headline: Life: the map you've explored is kept
details: On land and in the tribe stage, the parts of the island you've explored are now saved, so they stay uncovered when you close and reopen the game, and when your tribe starts.
At night the land you've explored stays faintly lit by the moon instead of going as dark as land you haven't seen.
Games saved before this update start with the map dark one last time; from then on it's remembered.
